title: RRHF: Rank Responses to Align Language Models with Human Feedback without tears
layout_note: Prior method on the left, proposed one on the right, inside one dashed outer frame split by a dashed vertical rule; each half titled with a bold word in its top-left corner.
grouping: Colour families carry roles across both halves: models are large yellow (trained) or dark-gold (fixed) rounded boxes, generated text and scores are green pills, queries are lavender pills. In the right half the three score pills are grouped by a dashed green rectangle, and the responses and their scores use the same dark-to-light green shades so each response is tied to its score.
shapes_depth: Flat filled rounded rectangles, no outlines or shadows, white or dark bold text inside; models are large boxes with large bold names, data items are small fully rounded pills. Solid black elbow arrows for data flow; dashed black arrows for the feedback loops (advantage back into both trained models on the left, ranking back into the language model on the right).
proposed_highlight: The proposed half needs one yellow model box where the prior half has four model boxes; its outcome is stated in large bold black text beside the score group ('Align by ranking SFT from best'). The method names are the two bold half titles.
lesson: Keep one colour code for roles across both halves (models as large yellow/gold boxes, text as green pills, queries as lavender pills) so the reader can count the models each method needs, and shade one colour family dark-to-light to tie each candidate response to its score.
notes: 'other' element = the score pills (100 / 80 / 60) that encode a ranking. Venue and year from the PDF footer (NeurIPS 2023).

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: aligning LLMs with human feedback by ranking
taxonomy.note: architecture other = a single policy model scoring several sampled responses against a ranking, contrasted with PPO's four-model setup

core.what: PPO (left) and RRHF (right) side by side inside one dashed frame, ours on the right, so the four big model blocks of PPO set against RRHF's one Language Model and one scorer read as a difference in count

relations.form: two halves of equal width headed 'PPO' and 'RRHF' in bold, each laid out on its own grid rather than as identical panels
PPO: Query -> Language Model / Value Model -> Model Response / Value -> Reward and Reference Models -> Advantage, read bottom to top

RRHF: three query rows each paired with a response from a different source (expert, ChatGPT, model), a Human Label/Reward Model assigning 100/80/60, and a dashed-framed stack of Expert/ChatGPT/Model scores above the Language Model
dashed lines return the update signal: from Advantage around both sides to the Language and Value models in PPO, from 'Align by ranking SFT from best' to the Language Model in RRHF

channels.colour: yellow = trained models, mustard = frozen scoring/reference models, green shades = responses and their scores by source (dark expert, mid ChatGPT, light model), pale blue = query; green also fills PPO's Advantage and Value, so green means both 'response/score' and 'PPO signal'
channels.shape: large rounded rectangles = models, pills = data and scores
channels.line: solid = forward data, dashed = training update
channels.frame: one outer dashed frame for the figure; a green dashed frame groups the score stack

quality.strengths: the two methods sit side by side at equal width, and model blocks are large and data pills small, so PPO's extra models are visible at a glance; response source is coded by green shade consistently from response to score
quality.weaknesses: the ranking objective is a bold text label ('Align by ranking SFT from best') rather than drawn ranked pairs; only the ChatGPT row has an arrow into the Human Label/Reward Model; the long arrow from the scores up to the text crosses the empty right side; the two halves use different layouts so parts do not line up for comparison

insights.structure: One dashed outer frame split by a dashed vertical rule into a 'PPO' half (four model boxes in a 2x2 grid around Query, Model Response, Value and Advantage pills) and an 'RRHF' half (one Language Model box above three query-response rows and a Human Label/Reward Model box).
insights.data: Models are large yellow (trained) or dark-gold (fixed) rounded boxes, queries are lavender pills, responses and scores are green pills shaded dark-to-light, and scores are numeric pills 100/80/60.
insights.emphasis: The RRHF half needs a single yellow model where PPO needs four, and its takeaway is set in large bold black text 'Align by ranking SFT from best' beside a dashed green group of three score pills.
insights.flow: In PPO the query flows bottom-up into two models with a dashed Advantage loop back around the outer edges; in RRHF responses go right into the reward box, scores rise to the bold text, and a dashed arrow returns left into the Language Model.
insights.avoid: Yellow vs dark-gold is the only cue for trained vs fixed and is never keyed; colour roles should get a small legend or label.

arrangement.units: two panels inside one dashed frame separated by a dashed vertical rule, each titled by a bold method name at its top-left
arrangement.losses_at: top of each panel: Advantage pill at the top of PPO, the bold 'Align by ranking' statement at top-right of RRHF
arrangement.shared: the same colour code for models, responses and queries across both panels
